title: Put a civilian on police negotiating teams, jury urges
article: A coroner's jury examining the death of a La Ronge man who was killed in a hail of police bullets two years ago has recommended that police negotiating teams include one person who's not a police officer.
As well, a negotiating team should be designated to contact family and friends of someone involved in a standoff, the jury said as the Shawn Martinot inquest wrapped up Tuesday.
Martinot died after a police standoff at the hotel where he worked in the northern Saskatchewan town.
He suffered 16 gunshot wounds in August 2004 after smashing vending machines and confronting police with a gun, the inquest heard.
Over the past week, witnesses testified the 38-year-old was drinking the day before the incident at the Northland Hotel, where Martinot also lived.
Tests later found traces of an antidepressant in his bloodstream.
A co-worker testified she became scared when Martinot began smashing vending machines with a sledgehammer. He also had a rifle next to him at his table.
Police came to the hotel and a 17-hour standoff began.
The RCMP fired tear gas at Martinot and sent in a robot, but he shot and disabled the device.
Martinot eventually came into the hallway where police were waiting. He had a gun in his hands and police shot him.
His mother, Gladys Martinot, told the inquest she would have come to the the scene and tried to reason with her son if anybody had contacted her in Flin Flon, Man.
